note: Official sources only. SHA256 is either the publisher's own published hash, or (documented below) a locally computed hash pinned after a manually verified HTTPS download of the official release, per docs/HARDWARE_STABILITY_SPEC.md section 3.

memorychecker.name: Memory Checker
memorychecker.sha256Source: locally computed from the official GitHub Releases HTTPS asset (no publisher-provided SHA256; only a custom .sig2 signature is offered)

prime95.name: Prime95 (GIMPS)
prime95.sha256Source: locally computed from the official mersenne.ca HTTPS mirror linked from mersenne.org/download (no publisher-provided SHA256)
prime95.license: Freeware (GIMPS End User License Agreement, mersenne.org/legal)

memtest_vulkan.name: memtest_vulkan
memtest_vulkan.sha256Source: locally computed from the official GitHub Releases HTTPS asset (no publisher-provided SHA256 file in this release)

smartmontools.name: smartmontools
smartmontools.md5Source: officially published by smartmontools.org / SourceForge (smartmontools-7.5.win32-setup.exe.md5); no SHA256 published for this release, so the publisher's own MD5 is used as the integrity check

librehardwaremonitor.name: LibreHardwareMonitorLib
librehardwaremonitor.sha256Source: locally computed from the official nuget.org HTTPS package endpoint (no separate publisher SHA256 file offered outside NuGet's own package signing)
librehardwaremonitor.notes: Optional dependencies DiskInfoToolkit and RAMSPDToolkit-NDD are not bundled/downloaded; Computer.IsStorageEnabled and Computer.IsMemoryEnabled are therefore left false (see Telemetry.psm1) so Open() does not abort before enumerating CPU/GPU/Motherboard hardware. Storage temperature is read from smartctl instead.
